# Target E: no greatest sufficient output orbit

Date: 2026-11-12. Author: proteinfolding-gpt / GPT Work.
Status: analytical draft, independently unreviewed when frozen.
Native bridge **NOT_DERIVED**; physical result **Not claimed**; scientific_breakthrough=false.

## 1. Question and scope

T-426 section 6 explicitly leaves open whether a greatest sufficient homogeneous orbit exists when premises are compared by their **actual allowed outputs**, rather than by subgroup inclusion. Its controlled-unitary witness has an orbit contained in the local-unitary orbit, so its subgroup argument does not settle this question. That limitation was already disclosed; it is not a newly discovered error.

Here the answer is **no**, even if every allowed group is connected. The proof is elementary: a sequence of compact connected sufficient orbits contains a sequence converging to a blind output. No closed sufficient set can contain all of them.

This result is about the supplied language below. It does **not** prove that no maximal sufficient orbit exists, that every pair of sufficient orbits lacks a common sufficient upper bound, that every premise language lacks a weakest member, or that native delivery is impossible. A greatest element and a maximal element are different notions.

## 2. Fixed benchmark and supplied premise language

All objects in this section are **SUPPLIED analytical benchmark choices**, or previously established mathematical consequences of those choices. No inherited native operation is asserted to produce them.

The source basis is \(X=(o,p,u,v)\); the retained-source basis is \(Y=(o,p,v)\). With \(Q:X\to Y\) the coordinate deletion map, the stipulated channel and source pair are
\[
\mathcal C(\rho)=Q\rho Q^\dagger+\rho_{uu}|p\rangle\langle p|,
\quad
\rho_+=\operatorname{diag}(1,1,2,1)/5,
\quad
\rho_-=\operatorname{diag}(1,1,1,2)/5.
\]
The complement has fixed factorization \(K=E\otimes R=\mathbb C^2\otimes\mathbb C^2\), in basis \(00,01,10,11\). For an orthonormal pair \((e_0,e_u)\), define
\[
W|j\rangle=|j\rangle|e_0\rangle\ (j=o,p,v),\qquad
W|u\rangle=|p\rangle|e_u\rangle.
\]
Orthogonality ensures that every such \(W\) realizes exactly \(\mathcal C\). The reference \(W_R\) uses \(e_0=|00\rangle,e_u=|01\rangle\).

Write \(\tau_j=\operatorname{Tr}_E|e_j\rangle\langle e_j|\). For the stipulated pair,
\[
d_R(W)=\frac15 D(\tau_u,\tau_0),\qquad
D(\alpha,\beta)=\tfrac12\|\alpha-\beta\|_1,
\quad
\mathcal B_R=\{W:\tau_u=\tau_0\}.
\]
This is optimized proper-\(R\) distinguishability. A single fixed binary effect for a whole orbit is a different condition.

**Declared language.** For every closed subgroup \(H\le U(K)\), admit the output set
\[
\mathcal O_H=\{(I_Y\otimes h)W_R:h\in H\}.
\]
Two groups with the same orbit represent the same premise. A premise is sufficient iff \(\mathcal O_H\cap\mathcal B_R=\varnothing\). A premise is weaker when its **orbit set** is larger. A greatest sufficient orbit must contain every sufficient orbit in this language. Also consider the restricted language in which \(H\) is connected. These language, topology and order choices are **SUPPLIED**, not native laws.

## 3. A connected structural family with a sharp positive margin

Let
\[
L=\{A\otimes B:A,B\in U(2)\},\quad
\zeta_t=\frac{1-t^2+2it}{1+t^2},\quad
V_t=\operatorname{diag}(1,1,1,\zeta_t),\quad
H_t=V_tLV_t^\dagger,\qquad 0\le t<\infty.
\]
Because \(|\zeta_t|=1\), each \(V_t\) is unitary. The group \(L\) is the continuous image of compact connected \(U(2)\times U(2)\); it is compact, hence closed, and connected. Conjugation preserves those properties, so every \(H_t\) belongs to both declared languages. This needs no classification of Lie subgroups.

Since \(V_t^\dagger\) fixes both \(00\) and \(01\), every member of \(\mathcal O_{H_t}\) has markers
\[
e_j=V_t(a\otimes b_j),\qquad
\|a\|=1,\quad (b_0,b_u)\text{ an orthonormal basis of }\mathbb C^2.
\]
Set \(p=|\langle0|a\rangle|^2\), and \(Z_t=\operatorname{diag}(1,\zeta_t)\). Then
\[
\tau_j=p|b_j\rangle\langle b_j|+
 (1-p)Z_t|b_j\rangle\langle b_j|Z_t^\dagger.
\]
The difference \(B=|b_u\rangle\langle b_u|-|b_0\rangle\langle b_0|\) has form
\[
B=\begin{pmatrix}z&w\\\bar w&-z\end{pmatrix},
\quad z\in[-1,1],\quad z^2+|w|^2=1.
\]
Its diagonal is unchanged by this mixture; the off-diagonal is multiplied by \(p+(1-p)\bar\zeta_t\). Therefore
\[
D(\tau_u,\tau_0)^2
 =z^2+\left|p+(1-p)\zeta_t\right|^2(1-z^2),
\]
\[
\left|p+(1-p)\zeta_t\right|^2
 =\frac{1+(2p-1)^2t^2}{1+t^2}
 \ge\frac1{1+t^2}.
\]
In particular,
\[
D(\tau_u,\tau_0)^2-\frac1{1+t^2}
 =\frac{t^2}{1+t^2}
 \left[z^2+(2p-1)^2(1-z^2)\right]\ge0.
\]
The ranges just stated make each term nonnegative. Equality is attained at \(p=1/2,z=0\). Thus the sharp orbit-wide margin is
\[
\boxed{\min_{W\in\mathcal O_{H_t}}d_R(W)
       =\frac1{5\sqrt{1+t^2}}>0\quad(t<\infty).}
\]
Every \(\mathcal O_{H_t}\) is sufficient. This sharp bound is a mathematical property of these supplied orbits; it adds no minimum signal-size requirement to the native target.

## 4. Blind accumulation point and no greatest orbit

Choose the Hadamard unitary \(F\) on both factors. The element \(h_t=V_t(F\otimes F)V_t^\dagger\) lies in \(H_t\) and sends the reference markers to
\[
e_0(t)=\tfrac12(1,1,1,\zeta_t)^\top,\qquad
e_u(t)=\tfrac12(1,-1,1,-\zeta_t)^\top.
\]
Their proper-\(R\) marginals are
\[
\tau_0(t)=\begin{pmatrix}
1/2&(1+\bar\zeta_t)/4\\
(1+\zeta_t)/4&1/2
\end{pmatrix},\qquad
\tau_u(t)=I_2-\tau_0(t).
\]
These attain the bound of section 3. For the sequence \(t=n\to\infty\), \(\zeta_n\to-1\), so
\[
e_0(\infty)=\tfrac12(1,1,1,-1)^\top,\qquad
e_u(\infty)=\tfrac12(1,-1,1,1)^\top.
\]
The limit markers remain orthonormal, the limiting isometry still realizes \(\mathcal C\), and both marginals equal \(I_2/2\). Hence \(W_\infty\in\mathcal B_R\).

Suppose a greatest sufficient orbit \(\mathcal O_*\) exists. It must contain \(\mathcal O_{H_n}\) for every positive integer \(n\), hence the selected \(W_n\). Every closed subgroup of the compact group \(U(4)\) is compact, and its orbit is compact, hence closed in the finite-dimensional isometry space. Consequently \(W_\infty\in\mathcal O_*\), contradicting sufficiency.

The same argument applies in the connected sublanguage, because each witness \(H_n\) is connected. **No step infers subgroup containment from orbit containment.** In fact the family has no common closed sufficient superset at all, a stronger upper-bound obstruction for this particular infinite family.

## 5. Controls and limits

At the limiting phase \(V_\infty=\operatorname{diag}(1,1,1,-1)\), the group \(V_\infty L V_\infty^\dagger\) remains compact and connected, but its orbit contains the blind point just exhibited. Thus compactness, connectedness, group structure, and global orthogonality alone do not force a proper-\(R\) signal. Every finite member of the sequence has a positive margin; its infimum over the sequence is zero. These quantifiers are not interchangeable.

For all dilations above, including the blind limit, the retained-source effect \(|p\rangle\langle p|\otimes I_K\) still has contrast \(1/5\). This result does not obstruct that separate owner-\(p\) route.

Every orbit here contains the \(R\)-rotation family \((I_E\otimes U_R)W_R\): take \(A=I_E,B=U_R\) inside the conjugated group. Therefore Dot's previously reviewed fixed-binary-effect control applies. These orbits do not have one common distinguishing binary effect. This does **not** exclude an informationally complete multi-outcome measurement or an effect family, and no new impossibility result about such measurements is claimed.

The constructive family is specified by conjugated local groups, not by defining each group to exclude the blind set. Nevertheless its phase, factorization, action and operational availability remain supplied. Nothing here derives a native event, source preparability, owner access, a physical clock, or receiver delivery. The useful conclusion is limited: changing from subgroup order to actual output-set order does not rescue a weakest sufficient premise in this chosen language. A new state/action/access clause must earn its own provenance; repeated group-label minimization does not earn it.

## 6. Evidence and inspected sources

- PREREG.md and check.py were frozen and exactly read back at b87165c31e0566b2bc6aa0d57a0d6b3666a7de1c before the checker ran. Checker blob 64e1a5ed174be415254a67c63f5a3e995538b9e0; preregistration blob 0175875657534d9b38d5c146d6630f6a845eb5ca.
- CHECKS.json records exact symbolic checks, all 16 matrix units for the selected finite family and again for its blind limit, the lower-bound identity, five rational squared contrasts, and the retained-\(p\) control. SymPy 1.14.0. No random sample, infinite group enumeration, native-event simulation, or inherited-stack recertification is claimed. The universal orbit and compactness statements are the proofs above, not extrapolations from finite runs.
- T-426 sections 2, 3, 5, 6 were read in full at thread commit 71ad62ea1db554897d46dbdf44ce7fcd29d4deaa; the associated Q185 RESULT.md was read at research commit f7fc6ad4c02c3069b7b2be315c22e34448c1e44b, blob 443eb25c5356832a787c3ca75d0b49ecddbf7938. Its Lie-theory claims are not dependencies of this proof and are not independently accepted here.
- TARGET_E_CLOSED_PREMISE_CHECK_2026_11_12.md, sections 1–6, frozen at 6c9be7cc12b8810bdf76ac12d6d8e2cda5a25e18, blob 8d124f818381c62620304bdae7293952a96d22cd, supplies the benchmark definitions and reviewed quantifier controls. Its independent review is run 43217169237 attempt 1. That acceptance does not extend to this new result until a separate review says so.

No scientific or literary novelty claim, numbered-stage certification, new branch, merge, or hold change.

"""Exact algebra audit of the supplied orbit-order example; not an exhaustive group test."""
import json
import sympy as s

t,p,z=s.symbols('t p z', real=True)
ii=s.I
zeta=(1-t*t+2*ii*t)/(1+t*t)
checks=[]

def zero(value):
    if isinstance(value,s.MatrixBase):
        return all(s.simplify(x)==0 for x in value)
    return s.simplify(value)==0

def check(name, condition):
    if not condition:
        raise AssertionError(name)
    checks.append(name)

def ptrace_k(matrix):
    return s.Matrix(3,3,lambda a,b:sum(matrix[4*a+k,4*b+k] for k in range(4)))

def ptrace_e(matrix):
    return s.Matrix(2,2,lambda a,b:sum(matrix[2*e+a,2*e+b] for e in range(2)))

def dilation(a,b):
    # Source order o,p,u,v. Retained-source order o,p,v.
    w=s.zeros(12,4)
    for j,out in [(0,0),(1,1),(3,2)]:
        for k in range(4): w[4*out+k,j]=a[k]
    for k in range(4): w[4+k,2]=b[k]
    return w

def target_channel(rho):
    result=rho.extract([0,1,3],[0,1,3])
    result[1,1]+=rho[2,2]
    return result

def channel_units(w):
    for a in range(4):
        for b in range(4):
            unit=s.zeros(4);unit[a,b]=1
            if not zero(ptrace_k(w*unit*w.H)-target_channel(unit)):
                return False
    return True

check('unit_phase_symbolic',zero(zeta*s.conjugate(zeta)-1))
a=s.Matrix([1,1,1,zeta])/2
b=s.Matrix([1,-1,1,-zeta])/2
check('marker_norms_and_orthogonality_symbolic',
      zero(a.H*a-s.eye(1)) and zero(b.H*b-s.eye(1)) and zero(a.H*b))
w=dilation(a,b)
check('isometry_symbolic',zero(w.H*w-s.eye(4)))
check('channel_all_16_matrix_units_symbolic',channel_units(w))

tau0=ptrace_e(a*a.H); tauu=ptrace_e(b*b.H)
delta=tauu-tau0
check('hadamard_pair_marginals_symbolic',zero(tau0-s.Matrix([
    [s.Rational(1,2),(1+s.conjugate(zeta))/4],
    [(1+zeta)/4,s.Rational(1,2)]])) and zero(tauu-(s.eye(2)-tau0)))
# For a traceless Hermitian 2x2 difference, D^2 = -det(delta).
d2=s.simplify(-delta.det()/25)
check('sharp_squared_margin_symbolic',zero(d2-1/(25*(1+t*t))))

q=p+(1-p)*zeta
q2=s.simplify(q*s.conjugate(q))
check('arbitrary_product_pair_phase_multiplier_symbolic',
      zero(q2-(1+(2*p-1)**2*t*t)/(1+t*t)))
excess=s.simplify(z*z+q2*(1-z*z)-1/(1+t*t))
check('all_orbit_members_lower_bound_identity',zero(excess-
      t*t/(1+t*t)*(z*z+(2*p-1)**2*(1-z*z))))
# Nonnegativity uses the explicitly declared ranges 0<=p<=1, -1<=z<=1.
values={str(n):str(s.factor(d2.subs(t,n))) for n in [0,1,2,10,1000]}
check('five_exact_sequence_values',all(s.Rational(v)>0 for v in values.values()))
check('phase_limit_minus_one',s.limit(zeta,t,s.oo)==-1)

a_inf=s.Matrix([1,1,1,-1])/2
b_inf=s.Matrix([1,-1,1,1])/2
w_inf=dilation(a_inf,b_inf)
check('blind_endpoint_is_orthonormal_isometry',zero(w_inf.H*w_inf-s.eye(4)))
check('blind_endpoint_preserves_all_16_channel_units',channel_units(w_inf))
check('adverse_control_orthogonality_does_not_imply_R_signal',
      zero(ptrace_e(a_inf*a_inf.H)-s.eye(2)/2) and
      zero(ptrace_e(b_inf*b_inf.H)-s.eye(2)/2))

rho_plus=s.diag(1,1,2,1)/5
rho_minus=s.diag(1,1,1,2)/5
owner=s.diag(0,1,0)
for label,ww in [('finite',w),('blind_limit',w_inf)]:
    contrast=s.trace(owner*ptrace_k(ww*(rho_plus-rho_minus)*ww.H))
    check('retained_p_contrast_'+label,zero(contrast-s.Rational(1,5)))

print(json.dumps({'status':'PASS','checks':checks,'check_count':len(checks),
 'd_R_squared_exact_values':values,
 'symbolic_d_R_squared':'1/(25*(1+t^2))',
 'limitations':['Algebra checks do not enumerate the infinite group.',
 'Compactness, connectedness, universal group-orbit bound and the greatest-orbit argument are proved in RESULT.md.',
 'This is not a native-event simulation or inherited-stack recertification.'],
 'native_bridge':'NOT_DERIVED','scientific_breakthrough':False},indent=2,sort_keys=True))

{
  "check_count": 15,
  "checks": [
    "unit_phase_symbolic",
    "marker_norms_and_orthogonality_symbolic",
    "isometry_symbolic",
    "channel_all_16_matrix_units_symbolic",
    "hadamard_pair_marginals_symbolic",
    "sharp_squared_margin_symbolic",
    "arbitrary_product_pair_phase_multiplier_symbolic",
    "all_orbit_members_lower_bound_identity",
    "five_exact_sequence_values",
    "phase_limit_minus_one",
    "blind_endpoint_is_orthonormal_isometry",
    "blind_endpoint_preserves_all_16_channel_units",
    "adverse_control_orthogonality_does_not_imply_R_signal",
    "retained_p_contrast_finite",
    "retained_p_contrast_blind_limit"
  ],
  "d_R_squared_exact_values": {
    "0": "1/25",
    "1": "1/50",
    "10": "1/2525",
    "1000": "1/25000025",
    "2": "1/125"
  },
  "limitations": [
    "Algebra checks do not enumerate the infinite group.",
    "Compactness, connectedness, universal group-orbit bound and the greatest-orbit argument are proved in RESULT.md.",
    "This is not a native-event simulation or inherited-stack recertification."
  ],
  "native_bridge": "NOT_DERIVED",
  "scientific_breakthrough": false,
  "status": "PASS",
  "symbolic_d_R_squared": "1/(25*(1+t^2))"
}

# Target E: output-orbit order check

Date: 2026-11-12. Status: bounded analytical follow-up to T-426 section 6, not a numbered retained stage.

The supplied language consists of compact homogeneous output sets O_H = H W_R for closed subgroups H <= U(E tensor R). Compare their actual sets by inclusion; equal orbits count as the same premise. Sufficiency means O_H avoids the fixed proper-R blind set. Also consider the sublanguage with H connected.

Question: does this language have a greatest sufficient orbit? The proposed answer is no, including the connected sublanguage. This is stronger in scope than T-426's subgroup-order statement but does not claim absence of maximal orbits, a native impossibility theorem, or a universal statement over premise languages.

Proposed witness: L = U(2) tensor U(2), V_t = diag(1,1,1,zeta_t), zeta_t = (1-t^2+2it)/(1+t^2), 0 <= t < infinity; H_t = V_t L V_t^*. V_t fixes the reference pair |00>, |01>. Every H_t orbit is sufficient with sharp proper-R margin 1/(5 sqrt(1+t^2)). Its Hadamard-pair member converges to a blind pair as t -> infinity. Every closed orbit containing all these sufficient orbits would contain that blind limit.

Before running the checker, freeze this plan and checker in GitHub. The checker is an algebra audit, not the proof of the infinite group or limit claims. Expected checks: unit phase, orthonormal marker pair, exact channel on all 16 matrix units, symbolic marginal formula and sharp squared gap, five exact sequence values, blind endpoint with unchanged channel, and retained p-effect contrast 1/5. Adverse control: orthogonality and compact connected group structure still hold at the blind endpoint; these premises cannot be substituted for proper-R sufficiency.

The proof and all source/action/interface choices are SUPPLIED analytical benchmark content. No native producer, availability, new signal threshold, or fixed binary effect is derived. Native bridge NOT_DERIVED; physical result Not claimed; scientific_breakthrough=false. No claim of literary or scientific novelty.

# Q185 RESULT (2026-11-12 ~05:25 MST). Verdict: PASS. Target E, structural (subgroup) premise language. Research c55f0602; PR111 at 662 comments.
Prop 185.1 (in the SUPPLIED language "closed subgroups H ≤ U(K) acting on W_R", with weakness = subgroup inclusion, also SUPPLIED): there is no weakest sufficient premise, and this holds even if the language is restricted to CONNECTED subgroups.
(1) L = U(E)⊗U(R) is sufficient with uniform d = 1/5 (check (c): τ_u − τ_0 has trace 0 and det −1, so eigenvalues ±1). Maximal sufficient (cited sketch): su(4)/so(4) is an irreducible symmetric pair, so so(4) ≅ su(2)⊕su(2) is a maximal subalgebra. Hence a closed H ⊋ L either contains SU(4) or has identity component L, and then H ≤ N(L) = L⋊{1,SWAP}. But SWAP·W_R = W_E is blind.
(2) Ctrl_E = {|0><0|⊗U_0 + |1><1|⊗U_1} (connected, R-unitaries controlled by E) is sufficient: g|00> = |0>U_0|0> and g|01> = |0>U_0|1>, so the R-marginals are orthogonal and d = 1/5. It contains CZ = diag(1,1,1,−1), which is entangling, so Ctrl_E ⊄ L. (Its orbit lies inside L's orbit: in orbit-inclusion order it is weaker-or-equal, not incomparable. Stated.)
(3) A finite witness that also escapes L's ORBIT: H_3 = <G>, G = rotation by 2π/3 on span{|00>,|11>}. Check (b): G³ = I, d values 1/5, 1/20, 1/20; G|00> has Schmidt rank 2, so the orbit is not contained in L's orbit. Control (d): the π/2 analogue (Z_4) hits B_R (d = 0 at n = 1, 3).
(4) Every closed subgroup containing L and one entangling gate is U(K) (Brylinski & Brylinski 2002: all local gates plus any imprimitive two-qubit gate are exactly universal; CITED, not re-proved). U(K)·W_R ∋ W_E. So L and Ctrl_E (or L and H_3) have no sufficient common upper bound. Hence no greatest sufficient subgroup.
Also re-verified exactly: GPT's d_R(W_t) = 4t²/[5(1+t²)²] and the normalization of e_u(t) (check (a)).
Limits: in orbit-inclusion order, whether a greatest sufficient homogeneous orbit exists is NOT decided. (1) and (4) rest on cited Lie theory and universality. Neither the language nor the order is native. This is a premise-language limitation, not a physical no-go, and it adds no delivery mechanism. Consistent with Dot's quantifier control (L's orbit contains S_rot, so it has no common fixed effect). Retained π_p contrast stays 1/5 throughout.

# Target E: pointwise delivery, a uniform margin, and closed-premise minimality

Date: 2026-11-12 America/Phoenix. Author: GPT Work.
Research snapshot: `266f9dec2388f2550004ecbd606ca7e550be47da`; thread through T-425.
Authority for scope: the 04:34 MST Engineering ruling recorded in ACTIVE_RESEARCH_QUESTION.md at `42c95e3354eb77cc79046a24e5bd311d2f8bb844` releases a formal minimal-premise analysis of the actual W_R/W_E benchmark and closes Q155–Q184.

Status: **AUTHOR ANALYTICAL CHECK; unreviewed; no native premise earned.** This is a bounded mathematical check for the released Target E, not an admitted native producing operation, a numbered certification stage, or an adopted physical postulate. No scientific program was executed.

## 1. Deduplication and the exact question

The unrestricted realization-predicate version of Target E is already answered by [receiver_delivery_boundary/RESULT.md](receiver_delivery_boundary/RESULT.md), RD-6 (Git blob `a04f23b6f667cf61c32149b1f3bb6e0316e60377`). For the stipulated proper complementary receiver R, let

    d_R(W) = D(tau_u, tau_0)/5,
    tau_j = Tr_E |e_j><e_j|,
    B_R = {W : d_R(W)=0}.

Here D is trace distance and W ranges over the fixed benchmark isometries implementing C. A predicate forces pointwise delivery exactly when it excludes B_R. Calling that predicate the weakest delivery premise restates the target. The exact contrast formula also appears in [p1_receiver_location_resolution/RESULT.md](p1_receiver_location_resolution/RESULT.md), section 5 (blob `4182ba347f8c11bad63315ffa6395c496ddfa498`).

T-416 and the owner-action directive distinguish this proper-R problem from the retained-source p-effect. T-417 adds no operation removing that distinction. The owner-supported finite-effect/common-kernel result is a different, already analyzed premise class; it is not repeated here.

The additional question here is narrowly defined: if one restricts the premise language to **closed sets of admissible benchmark realizations**, does a weakest sufficient premise emerge? “Closed” refers to ordinary finite-dimensional matrix topology in this supplied Hilbert benchmark. It is a SUPPLIED analytical restriction on premise language, not an inferred native topology, continuity law, or physical robustness principle.

## 2. Exact control: positive in every realization does not imply a positive uniform margin

Use the existing carrier X=(o,p,u,v), retained Y=(o,p,v), pair z+=(1,1,2,1)/5 and z-=(1,1,1,2)/5, and complement K=E tensor R with basis |e r>. Fix e_0=|00>. For 0<t<=1 set

    e_u(t) = [(1-t^2)|10> + 2t|01>] / (1+t^2),
    W_t|j> = |j>|00>  for j in Y,
    W_t|u> = |p>|e_u(t)>.

Normalization follows from (1-t^2)^2+4t^2=(1+t^2)^2, and e_u(t) is orthogonal to e_0. Thus RD-0 applies: every W_t is an isometry implementing exactly the same reduced source channel C. No source pair, owner designation, factorization, or interface changes with t. W_1 is W_R, and the limit at t=0 is W_E.

Taking the E marginal gives

    tau_0 = |0><0|,
    tau_u(t) = [(1-t^2)^2 |0><0| + 4t^2 |1><1|]/(1+t^2)^2.

Consequently,

    d_R(W_t) = 4t^2 / [5(1+t^2)^2] > 0.

One fixed effect F=I_S tensor I_E tensor |1><1| attains this signed contrast for every t>0. Its pre-event expectation is zero in both preparations. This is therefore not an artifact of optimizing a different measurement for each realization.

Yet inf_{0<t<=1} d_R(W_t)=0. An entirely rational sequence suffices: at t=1/n,

    d_R(W_(1/n)) = 4n^2 / [5(n^2+1)^2] <= 4/(5n^2) -> 0.

The set {W_t:0<t<=1} excludes EVERY R-blind realization, including W_E, but has no positive uniform delivery margin. This does not contradict RD-6: pointwise nonzero delivery is precisely its predicate-language result. A claimed uniform positive margin needs an additional condition. No detectable-size threshold is imposed on Aaron's one-effect target by this observation.

## 3. Closed sufficient classes have a margin, but no weakest such class exists

Let Wcal be the full benchmark implementation class and G=Wcal minus B_R. Wcal is compact: RD-0 identifies it with the continuous image of the compact unitary group U(K), equivalently the finite-dimensional orthonormal-pair space. The function d_R is continuous.

If S is a nonempty closed subset of Wcal and S is contained in G, compactness gives

    min_{W in S} d_R(W) > 0.

This is a conditional consequence of CLOSEDNESS plus pointwise delivery. The open family in section 2 explains why closedness cannot simply be omitted.

Now declare the premise class precisely:

    C_closed = {S closed in Wcal : W_R belongs to S and S intersect B_R is empty}.

This class is nonempty: S={W_R} belongs to it and has contrast 1/5. A larger admitted set is a weaker premise. There is no inclusion-maximal member of C_closed, and hence no weakest sufficient premise in this language.
